steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The human body has over 600 skeletal muscles . For GCSE PE, you must know the location and function of the major muscles listed below. | Definition: Muscles work in antagonistic pairs - when one muscle contracts (shortens), the other relaxes (lengthens). This allows bones to move at joints in opposite directions. | Agonist (Prime Mover): The muscle that contracts to produce the desired movement. It is the main muscle responsible for the action. | Antagonist: The muscle that relaxes (lengthens) to allow the agonist to work. It may offer some controlled resistance to smooth the movement.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Name the antagonistic pair at the elbow joint and identify the agonist during flexion. | Explain the difference between concentric and eccentric isotonic contraction, giving a sporting example of each. | What is the role of a fixator muscle? Give an example from a sporting action.

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Agonist (Prime Mover), Antagonist, Fixator (Stabiliser), and one past-paper question.
